title: Can Dedicated CtE Analysis Improve the CTR-DRBG Bound?
summary: The current robustness bound includes a contribution from the Generalized Leftover Hash Lemma analysis of CtE; it remains unresolved whether dedicated guessing-advantage analysis can improve it.

formal_statement.body: The CTR-DRBG robustness bound contains a term approximately $\frac{\sqrt{p}\,q}{2^{\lambda/2}}$, arising from use of the Generalized Leftover Hash Lemma to analyze the guessing advantage of $\operatorname{CtE}[E,n]$. Determine whether a dedicated analysis of this guessing advantage can improve the term.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the NIST CTR-DRBG robustness bound and the guessing advantage of its CtE construction.
parameters: p and q: factors in the robustness-bound term
lambda: exponent parameter in the denominator
E and n: inputs to CtE
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a dedicated analysis of CtE's guessing advantage can improve the robustness-bound term.

progress.summary: In its discussion of bound tightness, the source attributes this term to use of the Generalized Leftover Hash Lemma in analyzing CtE's guessing advantage and states that it is unclear whether a dedicated analysis can improve it.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., Security Analysis of NIST CTR-DRBG
